component.name: Apache Axiom
component.description: StAX-based XML object model conforming to the W3C XML Information Set, with a SAX adapter, a self-contained MIME multipart parser for SOAP-with-Attachments / XOP / MTOM, a base64 utility, and pluggable implementations (axiom-impl LLOM and axiom-dom). Axiom is an in-process Java library, the underlying object model used by Apache Axis2, Apache WSS4J's bindings, and Apache Neethi: no daemon, no listening socket, no CLI. The threat model is that of a streaming XML parser plus DOM-like object model plus MIME multipart parser with caller-selectable hardening profiles (StAXParserConfiguration DEFAULT / STANDALONE / SOAP). Source document is a draft awaiting Axiom / Webservices PMC review.

externalReferences.comment: Source security threat model (draft); this file is a structured translation of it.

blueprints.name: Axiom embedded-library trust structure
blueprints.description: Trust structure described by the threat model: the embedding Java application or SOAP stack (which selects the StAXParserConfiguration profile and supplies factories) is trusted; the producer of the XML / SOAP / MIME bytes is the only attacker-controllable input position. Out of model: the SOAP stack (Axis2), the transport layer, XML schema validation, the underlying StAX parser (Woodstox, SJSXP, JDK), the build-time axiom-weaver, and WS-Security processing (WSS4J).

assets.name: Object model and builders (axiom-api, axiom-impl, axiom-dom)
assets.description: OMXMLBuilderFactory entry points, the core OM (OMElement, OMDocument, OMText), StAX wrappers, SAX adapter, and the bundled LLOM (axiom-impl) and DOM-view (axiom-dom) implementations. The parser hardening profile chosen at builder-call time (DEFAULT, STANDALONE, SOAP) shapes the security envelope.

assets.name: MIME multipart parser (MultipartBody)
assets.description: Self-contained MIME parser for SOAP-with-Attachments / XOP / MTOM: parses MIME framing and produces per-part streams. Targeted at SOAP attachments, not a complete email-style MIME parser; imposes no bound on total body size, per-part size, part count, or nesting depth.

assets.name: OMMetaFactoryLocator extension point
assets.description: Locator that loads the class named by the org.apache.axiom.om.OMMetaFactoryLocator system property (and OSGi service registry state) via Class.forName at JVM startup. A privilege-escalation surface if the property can be set by an untrusted actor; the system property is trusted by the model.

zones.name: Producers of XML / SOAP / MIME bytes
zones.description: The only attacker-controllable input position: whoever supplies the bytes handed to the builders, the MIME parser, or the base64 decoder.

zones.name: Embedding application process
zones.description: The embedding Java application or SOAP stack, its caller-supplied OMFactory / OMMetaFactory / XMLInputFactory / XMLOutputFactory / PartBlobFactory, and the JVM system properties and classpath. All trusted by construction.

assumptions.description: A conformant JDK and a working StAX provider on the classpath (Woodstox is the supported preferred provider; SJSXP and the JDK StAX implementation are also recognized). Defects intrinsic to the StAX implementation are out of model and reported upstream.

Axiom opens no listening sockets, spawns no child processes, installs no signal handlers, reads only a small set of documented system properties, and writes only to the OutputStream / Writer the caller hands in (negative claims awaiting maintainer ratification).

Caller-supplied factories (OMFactory, OMMetaFactory, XMLInputFactory, XMLOutputFactory, XMLResolver, PartBlobFactory) and the OMMetaFactoryLocator system property are part of the caller's trusted computing base.
In-process callers, co-tenants in a shared JVM, side-channel observers, and quantum adversaries are out of scope.

threats.name: DOCTYPE accepted through the SOAP profile (XXE / billion laughs)
threats.description: The SOAP profile (used by default by OMXMLBuilderFactory.createSOAPModelBuilder) disallows DOCTYPE declarations, since a SOAP message MUST NOT contain a Document Type Declaration. An inbound SOAP envelope containing a DOCTYPE that is parsed to completion without an exception, letting an XXE or billion-laughs payload trigger, violates claimed property P1 and is security-critical (VALID).

threats.name: External entity fetched despite the STANDALONE profile
threats.description: The STANDALONE profile sets IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false and installs a custom XMLResolver that returns empty content for any external resource. If a caller explicitly selected STANDALONE and an external entity reference still results in an HTTP fetch to the attacker URL, claimed property P2 is violated (security-critical, VALID).

threats.name: MIME part streams bleeding bytes across part boundaries
threats.description: The MIME multipart parser claims that per-Part streams do not bleed bytes from neighboring parts. If PartImpl.getInputStream() returns bytes past the boundary of its part, contaminating a neighboring part's body, the property is violated; this is security-critical when the parts cross a trust boundary (for example one part is signed or authenticated and a neighboring part is not).

threats.name: XXE / billion laughs via the DEFAULT parser profile
threats.description: The default OMXMLBuilderFactory.createOMBuilder(InputStream) resolves to StAXParserConfiguration.DEFAULT, which does not disable DTD support or external entities; it only enables CDATA reporting. The model documents no XXE defense on this path: callers handling untrusted non-SOAP XML must explicitly select STANDALONE. Whether a report shaped 'I called createOMBuilder on attacker bytes and an XXE worked' is a valid finding or out of model (caller documented as required to pick a hardened profile) is an open maintainer question (Q7, proposed answer: out of model).

threats.name: Attacks through a caller-supplied, mis-hardened XMLStreamReader or factory
threats.description: When the caller passes a pre-built XMLStreamReader (or their own XMLInputFactory via setStAXFactory), Axiom does not re-configure it: the caller's XMLInputFactory is the gate for XXE / DTD posture. A mis-hardened caller factory is the caller's problem; hostile OMFactory / OMMetaFactory / XMLInputFactory / XMLOutputFactory implementations are out of scope.

threats.name: Resource exhaustion via unbounded XML, MIME, or base64 input
threats.description: Axiom imposes no bound on input XML / SOAP / MIME size, on the number of MIME parts, on per-part size or nesting depth, or on the decoded size of a base64 payload; the StAX implementation may enforce its own limits. Bounding input size is explicitly the caller's responsibility (at the HTTP / transport layer and at the MIME layer). Compression bombs in base64 and MIME nesting bombs are attack classes Axiom does not single-handedly defend against.

threats.name: Privilege escalation via the OMMetaFactoryLocator system property
threats.description: A class named in the org.apache.axiom.om.OMMetaFactoryLocator system property is Class.forName-loaded into the running JVM. The system property is a trusted, JVM-startup-time decision; an untrusted actor able to set it (for example from a servlet-context init parameter) is outside the model. The misuse pattern is documented so operators lock the property down.

threats.name: Out-of-layer concerns: signature wrapping, SOAP routing, transport, validation
threats.description: Axiom provides no protection against XML signature wrapping (the WS-Security layer's concern, WSS4J), no SOAP / WSDL routing or dispatch (Axis2), no transport-layer security (there is no transport), no XML Schema validation, no data-at-rest protection, no constant-time guarantees, and no thread-safety claim for concurrent mutation of the same OMElement. Defects intrinsic to the underlying StAX implementation and the build-time axiom-weaver are likewise out of model.

trustBoundaries.name: Byte-parsing trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: The moment attacker-controllable XML / SOAP / MIME / base64 bytes are handed to an Axiom builder or parser. Which hardening applies depends on the StAXParserConfiguration profile the caller selected: SOAP blocks DOCTYPE, STANDALONE neuters external entities, DEFAULT does neither.

controls.name: SOAP parser profile disallows DOCTYPE
controls.description: StAXParserConfiguration.SOAP disallows DOCTYPE declarations at first encounter (a SOAP message MUST NOT contain a Document Type Declaration). OMXMLBuilderFactory.createSOAPModelBuilder installs this profile by default; overriding it to a less safe profile is the caller's choice.

controls.name: STANDALONE profile neuters external entities
controls.description: StAXParserConfiguration.STANDALONE sets IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false and installs a custom XMLResolver that returns empty content for any external resource. It is the hardened profile for general untrusted (non-SOAP) XML input and must be selected explicitly by the caller.

controls.name: Select the right hardening profile per input kind
controls.description: For SOAP input, use createSOAPModelBuilder (or pass StAXParserConfiguration.SOAP explicitly); for general untrusted XML input, explicitly pass StAXParserConfiguration.STANDALONE to createOMBuilder. The bare createOMBuilder(InputStream) defaults to a profile that does not disable XXE / DTD, and the DEFAULT profile name is a false friend: it is the baseline fidelity shape, not a hardened default.

controls.name: Harden caller-supplied XMLStreamReader factories
controls.description: When passing a pre-built XMLStreamReader, configure the source XMLInputFactory with SUPPORT_DTD=false and IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false; Axiom does not retroactively reconfigure caller-supplied readers. Treat any caller-installed OMFactory, XMLInputFactory, XMLOutputFactory, XMLResolver, or PartBlobFactory as part of the security TCB.

controls.name: Bound input sizes at the caller layer
controls.description: Bound the maximum input size at the caller's HTTP / transport layer, and bound MIME multipart total size, per-part size, and part count at the caller layer; Axiom imposes none. Do not let untrusted actors influence the Content-Type header whose boundary parameter the MIME parser keys on, and bound base64 decoder output at the caller.

controls.name: Set locator system properties only at trusted JVM startup
controls.description: Set the OMMetaFactoryLocator system property only at JVM startup from a trusted source; never from a servlet-context init parameter or other user-influenced configuration, since the named class is loaded into the running JVM.

controls.name: Route message-level security through WSS4J or equivalent
controls.description: For deployment shapes that ingest SOAP envelopes that may carry attachments, route signature-wrapping defense through WSS4J or an equivalent message-level security layer; Axiom is the object model, not the policy.
